item.title: Biwako Valley: Ropeway, Sky Views and Winter Slopes — Guide
item.description: Biwako Valley, on the Hira mountains above Otsu, is Shiga’s easiest mountain thrill: a ropeway climbs some 1,100 metres in about five minutes to a summit plateau with one of the finest panoramas in the Kansai region — the whole silver expanse of Lake Biwa spread out below. In the green season the draw is the cliff-edge ‘Biwako Terrace’, a café-lounge with infinity-style decks that seem to float over the lake, plus ziplines and treetop adventure courses; in winter the same slopes become a ski and snowboard resort within an hour of Kyoto, making it a rare day-trip peak for city-based visitors.

item.title: Hakuba: Nagano's Premier Ski and Mountain Resort — Guide
item.description: Hakuba is one of Japan’s premier ski and mountain resort areas, a cluster of interconnected ski resorts beneath the towering Northern Japan Alps that hosted several events during the 1998 Nagano Winter Olympics. Renowned for its abundant, reliable powder snow, extensive and varied terrain and a lively international resort scene, Hakuba draws skiers and snowboarders from around the world in winter, while the green season offers hiking, alpine scenery and outdoor activities amid the same dramatic mountain backdrop.

item.title: Shiga Kogen: Japan's Largest Ski Resort and Highland Plateau — Guide
item.description: Shiga Kogen is Japan’s largest interconnected ski resort, a vast highland area of linked ski slopes served by a single combined lift pass that hosted events during the 1998 Nagano Olympics, renowned for its high elevation and long, reliable snow season. Beyond winter, the same plateau is a designated UNESCO biosphere reserve, and in the green season its ponds, marshes, forests and hiking trails at over 1,500 metres offer cool highland nature, alpine plants and autumn foliage, making it a genuine year-round mountain destination.

item.title: Skiing at Dynaland & Hirugano: Gifu's Accessible Ski Resorts — Guide
item.description: The Gujo highlands in central Gifu are home to several accessible ski resorts, most notably Dynaland and the adjacent Takasu Snow Park, which connect to form one of the region’s largest ski areas with extensive, varied terrain and popular night skiing. Nearby Hirugano Kogen offers gentler, family-friendly slopes, and the whole area’s convenient location within easy reach of Nagoya and central Gifu makes it a popular winter destination for day trips and weekend visits from the surrounding region.

item.title: Kusatsu International Ski Resort: Powder Snow Meets Hot Spring — Guide
item.description: Kusatsu International Ski Resort combines reliable, high-quality powder snow with the rare advantage of Japan’s top-ranked hot spring town at its base, letting skiers and snowboarders soak away the day’s exertion in Kusatsu’s mineral-rich waters. The resort offers slopes suited to a range of skill levels, from gentle beginner runs to more challenging terrain, with panoramic views over the surrounding mountains from the higher lift stations on clear winter days.

item.title: Appi Kogen Resort: Tohoku's Powder & Highland Playground — Guide
item.description: Appi Kogen is one of Tohoku’s largest ski resorts — famed for long, well-groomed runs of light powder snow in winter, drawing skiers from across Japan and abroad. In summer the highland turns green for golf, hiking and family activities, making it a year-round mountain playground in northern Iwate. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Hachimantai, Iwate Hours Winter ski season; summer activities Admission Lift passes / activity fees vary Time needed Half–full day Best time Winter (powder); summer (highland) What to Do Long, groomed powder-snow ski runs in winter.

item.title: Niseko Guide: Skiing, Powder Snow & Season
item.description: Niseko is Japan’s most famous ski destination and a global byword for powder snow. Blessed with extraordinarily light, abundant “Japow” blown in off the Sea of Japan, this resort area on the flank of Mt. Niseko Annupuri — gazing across to the perfect cone of Mt. Yotei — draws skiers and snowboarders from around the world. Four interconnected ski areas, lively après-ski, world-class dining and superb onsen make it a winter resort like no other, while summer brings rafting, cycling and hiking in cool mountain air.
